objectives.en: Describe how DNA is isolated from bacterial, plant and fungal cells
Explain the three steps of PCR and the role of Taq polymerase

narration.en: A single drop of blood holds too little DNA to study. PCR copies a chosen stretch of it again and again until there are about a billion copies.
narration.kn: ಒಂದು ಹನಿ ರಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಧ್ಯಯನಕ್ಕೆ ಸಾಕಷ್ಟು DNA ಇರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. PCR ಆಯ್ದ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ನಕಲು ಮಾಡಿ ಸುಮಾರು ನೂರು ಕೋಟಿ ಪ್ರತಿಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: DNA is enclosed within membranes, so cells are broken open with enzymes: lysozyme for bacteria, cellulase for plant cells and chitinase for fungi. DNA is bound to histones and mixed with RNA and proteins, so the extract is treated with ribonuclease to remove RNA and protease to remove proteins. Purified DNA finally precipitates on adding chilled ethanol and can be seen as a collection of fine threads in the suspension, which can be spooled out. The purified DNA is then incubated with a restriction enzyme under optimal conditions, and agarose gel electrophoresis checks the digestion. The vector DNA is cut with the same enzyme, and the "cut" source DNA and vector are mixed with DNA ligase to make recombinant DNA.

points.en: RNase removes RNA; protease removes proteins
Chilled ethanol precipitates DNA as fine threads
Same restriction enzyme for source and vector, then ligase

narration.en: To isolate DNA we break the cell wall with lysozyme, cellulase or chitinase, remove RNA and proteins with ribonuclease and protease, and precipitate the DNA with chilled ethanol as fine threads. It is then cut and ligated into a vector.
narration.kn: DNA ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕಿಸಲು ಲೈಸೋಜೈಮ್, ಸೆಲ್ಯುಲೇಸ್ ಅಥವಾ ಕೈಟಿನೇಸ್‌ನಿಂದ ಕೋಶಭಿತ್ತಿ ಒಡೆದು, ರೈಬೋನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯೇಸ್ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರೋಟಿಯೇಸ್‌ನಿಂದ RNA ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ತೆಗೆದು, ತಣ್ಣನೆಯ ಎಥೆನಾಲ್‌ನಿಂದ DNA ಯನ್ನು ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮ ಎಳೆಗಳಾಗಿ ಹೊರತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ.

say.en: PCR copies a chosen piece of DNA again and again. Each cycle has three steps at three temperatures.
Heat separates the two strands; on cooling, two short primers bind to the ends of the target; then Taq polymerase extends them into new strands.
Every cycle doubles the number of copies, so after n cycles we have N naught times two to the power n.
From a single molecule, ten cycles give 1024 copies and thirty cycles about a billion.
The enzyme survives the 94 degree step because it comes from Thermus aquaticus, a bacterium of hot springs.

narration.en: PCR copies a chosen piece of DNA again and again. Each cycle has three steps at three temperatures. Heat separates the two strands; on cooling, two short primers bind to the ends of the target; then Taq polymerase extends them into new strands. Every cycle doubles the number of copies, so after n cycles we have N naught times two to the power n. From a single molecule, ten cycles give 1024 copies and thirty cycles about a billion. The enzyme survives the 94 degree step because it comes from Thermus aquaticus, a bacterium of hot springs.

body.en: PCR (polymerase chain reaction) makes multiple copies of a gene (DNA of interest) in vitro, using two sets of primers (small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides complementary to the regions of DNA at the ends of the target) and DNA polymerase. Each cycle has three steps: denaturation (the double-stranded DNA is separated by high temperature), annealing (primers bind to the single strands) and extension (the polymerase extends the primers using the nucleotides provided and the DNA as template). A thermostable DNA polymerase, Taq polymerase from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus, survives the high denaturation temperature. Since every cycle doubles the DNA, repeating the process many times amplifies the segment approximately a billion times. The amplified fragment can be ligated into a vector for cloning.

points.en: Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus: thermostable

narration.en: PCR copies a target stretch of DNA in a test tube. Each cycle has denaturation, annealing of primers and extension by the heat-stable Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus, and each cycle doubles the DNA.
narration.kn: PCR ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾನಳಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ಗುರಿ DNA ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ನಕಲು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಚಕ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಡಿನ್ಯಾಚುರೇಶನ್, ಪ್ರೈಮರ್ ಅನೀಲಿಂಗ್ ಮತ್ತು ಥರ್ಮಸ್ ಅಕ್ವಾಟಿಕಸ್‌ನ ಉಷ್ಣ-ಸ್ಥಿರ Taq ಪಾಲಿಮರೇಸ್‌ನಿಂದ ವಿಸ್ತರಣೆ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ; ಪ್ರತಿ ಚಕ್ರ DNA ಯನ್ನು ದ್ವಿಗುಣಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

aim.en: To make a qPCR standard curve, find the amplification efficiency and quantify an unknown sample.

narration.en: Run a PCR and watch the amount of DNA rise cycle by cycle. Samples that start with more DNA reach the threshold in fewer cycles.

caption.en: Copies grow as N = N0 × (1 + E)^n, where E is the efficiency of each cycle (100 % means perfect doubling). The graph shows log10 of the number of copies.

tryThis.en: Start from 1 copy with perfect doubling: how many cycles give a billion copies?
Drop the efficiency to 80 %. How many extra cycles are needed?
Start with 1000 copies. How many cycles do you save?

problem.en: A PCR starts with 1 molecule of double-stranded target DNA. Assuming perfect doubling, how many copies are present after 10 cycles, and after 30 cycles?

steps.en: Each cycle doubles the DNA: N = N₀ × 2ⁿ.

answer.en: 1,024 copies after 10 cycles; about 1.07 billion after 30 cycles.
